subject: SLO-driven pilot — cost/latency trade-offs and next steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@observerai.com>, Michael Long <michael.long@observerai.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 13:02:00 -0400
Subject: SLO-driven pilot — cost/latency trade-offs and next steps

Thanks again for a productive call this morning — appreciate the clear ask and the sample traffic profile you shared. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we can convert the pilot into a scoped SOW: 

Key points from the call:
- Target workload: conversational assistant that averages ~70 tokens/request and 3 requests/user/day (mostly short chat turns).
- Expected QPS shape: spiky daytime bursts (peak 22 QPS), baseline ~4 QPS.
- Data policy: inference-only, no retention beyond 24 hours (tenant-level KV only).

Cost and unit-econ starting assumptions I sketched during the call (attached workbook has line-by-line):
- Volume band: 30M–100M tokens/month initially; 6–9 months ramp window.
- Target unit price: customer indicated an internal goal around $35–$55 per 1M tokens.
- Reducing to $/1M requires trade-offs on SLOs + model variant choice; see options below.

Latency vs. cost trade-offs (recommendation):
1) Premium SLO (avg token latency <= 200ms; 95th percentile approx 300–350ms):
   - Use streaming + low-latency model variant (bigger model, FP16 or 4-bit optimized).
   - Expected unit cost: higher (roughly +25–40% vs baseline) due to reserved capacity and priority routing.
2) Balanced SLO (avg token latency 300–400ms):
   - Use small-medium model variant + aggressive batching during baseline; streaming for spikes.
   - Expected unit cost: midpoint; likely achievable to hit $40–$50 /1M with 50–100 token caches.
3) Cost-first (avg token latency 400ms+; tolerate tail):
   - Heavier batching, lower-reservation tier, fallback to cheaper quantized variant.
   - Expected unit cost: lowest; could approach $30–35 /1M at higher volumes but with noticeable tail-latency during spikes.

Suggested next steps:
- Kimberly/Grace: run a 2-week controlled pilot (we handle routing & caching config) — we’ll instrument token-level econ and latency SLOs.
- Asha/Michael: confirm the 30–100M token band and any absolute budget ceiling for month 1.
- Deliverables: pilot pricing workbook (attached), SLO playbook (attached), and a short canary run plan by Friday.

Attachments: pilot-pricing-workbook.xlsx (pricing scenarios), SLO-playbook.pdf (SLO tiers & measurement).

Thanks — I’ll schedule the follow-up action item review once you confirm budget band.

—Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO-driven pilot — cost/latency trade-offs and next steps

Thanks Kimberly — this is helpful and matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirming the monthly band: planning for a conservative 40M month-1, with potential jump to 85–95M by month 4 depending on user adoption.
- Budget: leadership has signaled an initial cap of $3,200/month for hosted inference during pilot (they want to understand unit economics before committing more).
- Latency tolerance: our product team wants steady <350ms P50 and <600ms P95 for primary user flows. They can accept ~800ms tails for non-critical batch summarization.

Actionable asks: 
1) Can you return a concrete pricing row that maps to our 40M starting point and the two SLO options (Balanced vs Cost-first) by EOD Thursday?
2) If we aim for the Balanced SLO, what model variant do you recommend to stay within $3.2k/month for 40M tokens (including any reserved capacity assumptions)?

Will loop in procurement if we get a firm pilot quote. Thanks — looking forward to the workbook numbers.

—Asha
Head of Product
ObserverAI

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2027 09:42:00 -0400
Subject: RE: SLO-driven pilot — cost/latency trade-offs and next steps

Kimberly — I started the workbook scenarios this morning. Notes for the quote rows (we need to be careful to surface assumptions):
- "Balanced SLO" scenario (target P50 ~300ms, P95 ~500ms):
  • Model: Redwood-variant-medium-q4 (quantized 4-bit) with occasional fallback to medium-fp16 for long contexts.
  • Routing: Dedicated small reserved pool + burst-to-hosted. Autoscale window 60s.
  • Expected blended unit cost: ~$48 /1M tokens at 40M volume (includes small reserved allocation & reserved burst buffer).
- "Cost-first" scenario (accept higher tails):
  • Model: medium-q4 w/ more aggressive batching and longer autoscale window (120s).
  • Expected blended unit cost: ~$34–36 /1M tokens at 40M.

Given ObserverAI's $3.2k/month budget for month 1: at 40M tokens that implies ~ $80 /1M which is inconsistent with their stated target — meaning they likely intend the $3.2k to cover only a portion of inference (or will pilot a smaller subset). Two options to propose back:
1) Narrow the pilot to a 8–12M token subset (e.g., beta cohort) and hit Balanced SLO within $3.2k.
2) Keep 40M scope but request a short term pilot credit / discounted reserved rate to show the baseline metrics and unit economics.

I can populate the two explicit quote rows and the delta to reach their stated SLOs — Kimberly, can you confirm discount levers we can offer for month-1 only?

—Grace
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@observerai.com>, Michael Long <michael.long@observerai.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO-driven pilot — cost/latency trade-offs and next steps

Asha — quick update and concrete asks so we can move to a signed pilot: 

1) Pricing rows: Grace/I will send two firm quote rows by EOD Thursday (Balanced SLO at 40M and Cost-first at 40M) with explicit assumptions called out.
2) Pilot sizing: we recommend option (1) from Grace — narrow pilot to ~10M token beta cohort to stay within the $3.2k pilot budget while demonstrating SLOs. That gives you reliable signals and keeps runway for month-1.
3) Short-term concession: we can provide a one-time pilot credit of $2,000 applied to month-1 if ObserverAI signs the pilot SOW within two weeks. That reduces your net spend and lets us show the SLO economics at scale.

Please confirm you are OK with the 10M scoped beta approach or whether leadership insists on the full 40M for month-1 (if so we will include a discounted reserved-rate quote to cover the gap). Also confirm whether procurement needs a separate statement of work template — I can loop Legal/GTM.

Next call? I have availability Friday 08 Jul 2027 10:00–11:00 PT if you want to walk the workbook live.

Thanks — looking forward to your direction.

—Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
